translationRepairs: In the fourth month of the third year (997), Jiao Wo, vice horse-and-arms commander of the Shenqi Army, presented coiled iron spears weighing fifteen jin; ordered to demonstrate them, he wheeled about on horseback as if flying, and was promoted to command that army.

In the fourth month of the third year (1000), Jiao Wo, vice horse-and-arms commander of the Shenqi Army, presented coiled iron spears weighing fifteen jin; ordered to demonstrate them, he wheeled about on horseback as if flying, and was promoted to command that army.
Immediate prior unit establishes 咸平元年, so unmarked 三年四月 is Xianping 3 (AD 1000); the parenthetical 997 wrongly treats the year as Zhidao 3.
In the fifth year (999), Liu Yongxi, commissioner of Ninghua Army, devised a hand cannon and presented it; the court ordered the border commands to build them for service.
In the fifth year (1002), Liu Yongxi, commissioner of Ninghua Army, devised a hand cannon and presented it; the court ordered the border commands to build them for service.
Under the continuing Xianping sequence after 咸平元年, 五年 is Xianping 5 (AD 1002), not 999.
In the tenth month of the sixth year (1001), message tokens were issued to the army.
In the tenth month of the sixth year (1003), message tokens were issued to the army.
六年十月 continues the same Xianping count, so the year is AD 1003, not 1001.
Wang An submitted a memorial: "Emperor Xuandi of Han is hailed as a restorative ruler, yet histories say skilled artisans flourished only under Emperors Yuan and Cheng.
Wang Pang submitted a memorial: "Emperor Xuandi of Han is hailed as a restorative ruler, yet histories say skilled artisans flourished only under Emperors Yuan and Cheng.
王雱 is Wang Pang; idiomatic Wang An wrongly collapses him with 王安石.
In sum, An's argument catered to the emperor's mood and sought rashly to overturn established practice.
In sum, Pang's argument catered to the emperor's mood and sought rashly to overturn established practice.
雱 names Wang Pang; An wrongly points to Wang Anshi.

Wang An argued that since antiquity the south had repeatedly beaten Chinese armies with elephants and that Shilong's plan deserved trial; he also expounded classical chariot doctrine and proposed a chariot-versus-cavalry test.

Wang Anshi argued that since antiquity the south had repeatedly beaten Chinese armies with elephants and that Shilong's plan deserved trial; he also expounded classical chariot doctrine and proposed a chariot-versus-cavalry test.
安石 is Wang Anshi; Wang An confuses him with 王雱.
Wang An said: "That is exactly right.
Wang Anshi said: "That is exactly right.
安石曰 attributes the speech to Wang Anshi, not Wang An.
Wang An added: "The court seeks only fairness in governance."
Wang Anshi added: "The court seeks only fairness in governance."
安石曰 again names Wang Anshi; Wang An is the wrong person.
In the end Wang An's rhetoric dispelled the emperor's doubts, and the directorate escaped charges of fraud.
In the end Wang Anshi's rhetoric dispelled the emperor's doubts, and the directorate escaped charges of fraud.
安石卒以辯口 is Wang Anshi’s rhetoric, not Wang An’s.
In the eighth month, at Zhao Zhi's request, Huanqing received one thousand divine-arm crossbows and one hundred thousand arrows.
In the eighth month, at Zhao Xie's request, Huanqing received one thousand divine-arm crossbows and one hundred thousand arrows.
趙禼 is romanized Zhao Xie; Zhi misreads 禼.
In Chongning 3 the Hebei and Shaanxi transport commissions reported: "If Xu Yankui's chariot pattern is used, the chariot is large and cost doubles.
In Chongning 3 the Hebei and Shaanxi transport commissions reported: "If Xu Yangui's chariot pattern is used, the chariot is large and cost doubles.
許彥圭 is Xu Yangui (圭 gui); Yankui misreads the given name.
The court nonetheless adopted Xu Yankui's design.
The court nonetheless adopted Xu Yangui's design.
許彥圭式 is Xu Yangui’s pattern, not Yankui’s.
These chariots reached the court through Yao Lin promoting Xu Yankui's design.
These chariots reached the court through Yao Lin promoting Xu Yangui's design.
許彥圭 is Xu Yangui; Yankui is an incorrect romanization.
Yankui sought only personal promotion at the state's expense; failure to punish him would invite repetition.
Yangui sought only personal promotion at the state's expense; failure to punish him would invite repetition.
彥圭 short-form should be Yangui, not Yankui.
彥圭 is Yangui; Yankui misreads 圭.
In the Jianyan era eunuch supervisor was briefly appointed then removed.
In the Jianyan era the eunuch Dong Que was briefly appointed supervisor then removed.
Chinese names the eunuch 董愨; the idiomatic omitted that personal name.
The court trusted Lin's frontier expertise, not realizing Yankui was reckless and Lin acted from private loyalty.
The court trusted Lin's frontier expertise, not realizing Yangui was reckless and Lin acted from private loyalty.
彥圭輕妄 refers to Yangui; Yankui is wrong.
Huaidong chief steward Zhu Qian reported: "The Jiangdu army is Han Shizhong's old command.
Huaidong chief steward Zhu Qian reported: "The Zhenjiang army is Han Shizhong's old command.
鎮江一軍 is the Zhenjiang army; Jiangdu (江都) is absent from the Chinese.
Huaidong chief steward Zhu Qian said: "The Jiangdu army is Han Shizhong's old command.
Huaidong chief steward Zhu Qian said: "The Zhenjiang army is Han Shizhong's old command.
Literal likewise misreads 鎮江 as Jiangdu; Zhenjiang is required.
He counted 8,842 crossbowmen needing 17,684 bows but found only 6,574 serviceable and asked Jiangdu headquarters to fill the gap."
He counted 8,842 crossbowmen needing 17,684 bows but found only 6,574 serviceable and asked Zhenjiang headquarters to fill the gap."
乞下鎮江都統司 names the Zhenjiang command headquarters, not Jiangdu.

Now examining the various armies' present crossbowmen eight thousand eight hundred forty-two men, each man should use two bows—one bow for daily drill, one bow prepared for battle—altogether should use seventeen thousand six hundred eighty-four bows; only six thousand five hundred seventy-four remain, the rest all unfit for drill instruction; we beg the Jiangdu command headquarters fill the quota."

Now examining the various armies' present crossbowmen eight thousand eight hundred forty-two men, each man should use two bows—one bow for daily drill, one bow prepared for battle—altogether should use seventeen thousand six hundred eighty-four bows; only six thousand five hundred seventy-four remain, the rest all unfit for drill instruction; we beg the Zhenjiang command headquarters fill the quota."
Literal 鎮江都統司 must be Zhenjiang command headquarters, not Jiangdu.
Before long Commandery-Manufacture Wu Ting memorialized: "The divine-power bow with pellet-head arrows—in the armies' use it is truly convenient and swift; the divine-arm cannot match it."
Before long Overall Commander Wu Ting memorialized: "The divine-power bow with pellet-head arrows—in the armies' use it is truly convenient and swift; the divine-arm cannot match it."
都統製 is the overall-commander title; Commandery-Manufacture invents an office absent from the Chinese.
Lamellae outside specified weights were discarded as waste.
If lamellae were required one by one to match the originally allotted weights, whenever heavy and light differed they were discarded unused, wasting labor and materials.
若甲葉一一依元領分兩…即棄不用 states that strict per-lamella weight matching caused wasteful discards; the shorter idiomatic omitted that condition.

They also made fire-lance guns, using the world's bamboo as tubes, installing pellet nests inside; when fired like a torch, after the flame died the pellet nest shot out like cannon sound, heard more than one hundred fifty paces distant.

They also made fire-lance guns, using bamboo as tubes, installing pellet nests inside; when fired like a torch, after the flame died the pellet nest shot out like cannon sound, heard more than one hundred fifty paces distant.
以世竹為筒 means using bamboo as the tube; “the world’s bamboo” invents a false literal sense for 世.
